prompt: A call-center app needs guaranteed throughput and steady latency at peak hours, and expects heavy predictable traffic.
why: Provisioned throughput reserves capacity for predictable, heavy load.
trap: A smaller model is faster, but doesn't guarantee capacity.

prompt: Regulations require that prompts and responses are processed only within the EU.
why: A data-zone deployment keeps processing inside a geography.
trap: Privacy is the principle; choosing the deployment type is how you meet it.

prompt: Each night, 500,000 product descriptions need rewriting, and nobody needs results until morning.
why: A batch deployment processes large jobs asynchronously at lower cost.
trap: Cheaper models help too, but the hosting choice is batch.

prompt: A prototype gets a few calls a day with unpredictable spikes, and the team wants to pay only for what it uses.
tells: pay only for what it uses
why: A standard (pay-per-token) deployment fits low, spiky usage.
trap: Provisioned throughput charges for reserved capacity even when idle.

prompt: A startup wants the highest available capacity with no reserved commitment, and doesn't mind requests being processed in any Azure region.
why: A global standard deployment routes to any region for the best capacity, pay-as-you-go.
trap: Data-zone deployments are for when data must stay in a geography.

prompt: Traffic is steady at millions of tokens every hour, and finance wants a predictable monthly bill instead of per-token charges.
why: Provisioned throughput gives fixed-price reserved capacity for steady heavy use.
trap: Capping tokens limits replies; it doesn't change how you're billed.
